findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with nil TopicUser when the user has no topic_user record
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level`. For any logged-in user who never viewed/posted/tracked the topic (e.g. they were watching via a category default or received the email via a group mention), no topic_users row exists, so `tu` is nil and the action raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing the user. It should use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` which creates the record when missing.

findings.title: State-changing GET endpoint can be triggered by email scanners/link prefetchers
findings.body: The unsubscribe link in emails is a plain GET to /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe that immediately mutates the user's notification level (topics_controller.rb line 98-116, route added in config/routes.rb line 440-441). Mail clients and security scanners (antivirus proxies, Gmail link scanning, Apple Mail prefetch) routinely GET links in emails without the user clicking them. Any such scan silently mutes the user's topic, or worse toggles them to regular, without consent. Standard practice (and what the existing /email/unsubscribe/:key flow does) is a token-authenticated link or a confirmation page; this endpoint requires only a logged-in session and a guessable numeric topic id, and it also lets any logged-in user flip their own state via CSRF-free GET from any page (img tag on any site they visit while logged in, since there is no CSRF check on GET).

findings.title: Direct save of TopicUser skips notifications_changed_at, reason, and MessageBus updates
findings.body: The unsubscribe action assigns `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. TopicUser.change is the canonical path: it sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (so the UI shows why the level changed) and publishes a `notification_level_change` MessageBus message to /topic/:id so open tabs update. Saving directly leaves the reason stale (e.g. still 'auto_watch') and other clients' UIs out of sync. Also, an unsubscribe click when the level is 'regular' or below sets it to 'muted', but when it is 'tracking'/'watching' it only drops to 'regular' — a 'regular' user still receives replied-to/mentioned notifications for that topic, so the email's promise 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' (config/locales/server.en.yml) is not kept for those users.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} for all callers of MessageBuilder
findings.body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` locale string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#body` (lib/email/message_builder.rb line 90) and `#html_part` (line 67) render this string with `template_args` for any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`; any other caller (plugins, themes, or future core mailers) that enables `add_unsubscribe_link` without supplying `unsubscribe_url` will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and the email will fail to build. A safer design keeps the per-topic sentence in a separate translation or makes the segment conditional.

findings.title: topicUnsubscribe client route is shadowed by the topic resource's fromParamsNear route
findings.body: The new route `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' })` is registered after `this.resource('topic', { path: '/t/:slug/:id' }, ...)` whose child route `fromParamsNear` has path '/:nearPost' (a wildcard segment). Because the topic resource is declared first, a URL like /t/my-slug/123/unsubscribe can be matched by topic.fromParamsNear with nearPost='unsubscribe', loading the full topic instead of the unsubscribe page. The unsubscribe route needs to be registered before the topic resource (or the nearPost segment constrained to digits) so it takes precedence.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe controller action or route
findings.body: The PR adds a new mutating endpoint (TopicsController#unsubscribe), new routes, a mailer change, and a locale change, but the only test modification is passing `unsubscribe_url` to an existing MessageBuilder spec. There are no request specs covering: successful unsubscribe, the nil-TopicUser case, the slug redirect branch, or the toggle logic (watching → regular, regular → muted). Given the nil-crash and the mute-vs-regular semantics questions above, these behaviors need test coverage before merging.
